cohort: The study included 10,253 pregnant women and neonates born at Shenmu Hospital in China between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2023, divided into a macrosomia group (n=1100) and a normal-weight control group (n=9153).
finding: Male neonates, higher gestational age, maternal height >=165 cm, prepregnancy obesity, excessive weight gain, multiparity, gestational diabetes, and excess amniotic fluid were associated with an increased risk of macrosomia, while scarred uterus, gestational hypertension, oligohydramnios, and umbilical cord anomalies were associated with a decreased risk.
birth_weight: Macrosomia cases were defined as birth weight >=4000 g, and controls as birth weight 2500-3999 g.
gest_age: Gestational age was identified as a risk factor for macrosomia, but specific inclusion criteria based on gestational age were not mentioned.
